incidents.victim: France — Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: Attacker misused a stolen or spoofed identity to reach internal servers, then connected through the agency's VPN and used an internal lookup tool to search and extract taxpayer records.
incidents.impact: France's tax authority confirmed data on individuals and businesses was viewed and extracted; a hacker using the alias ZeroBytes claims 600,000 people were affected, including names, tax IDs, email addresses and tax-status details. Access was detected and cut off in late June.

incidents.vector: A single suspected advanced-persistent-threat actor exploited critical directory-traversal flaw CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8) for remote code execution on internet-reachable vCenter, then installed reverse_ssh for persistence that survives patching.
incidents.impact: Incident responders at QUIRSO traced global exploitation to 361 unique IP addresses across 47 countries (US, France, Iran and Turkey most targeted), beginning less than a week after the July 29 disclosure; new victims are still being observed.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government networks and Thailand Ministry of Finance
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese operators used publicly available AI tooling (a framework of Hermes and OpenClaw agents) to automate reconnaissance, initial access, lateral movement and data exfiltration in a largely autonomous intrusion.
incidents.impact: Described as the first observed 'near-autonomous' AI-driven attack on a government target; part of a broader wave hitting multiple Asian government networks, including the breach of Thailand's finance ministry.

incidents.victim: Goodwin Procter and WilmerHale (US law firms)
incidents.vector: The Silent Ransom group (aka Luna Moth) posed as IT support staff — increasingly in person — and had victims install legitimate remote-access software, then rapidly exfiltrated sensitive data, often completing the whole operation in a single day.
incidents.impact: Two major law firms reportedly paid substantial ransoms this year — Goodwin Procter about $10 million and WilmerHale about $18 million — reflecting the booming shift toward data-theft extortion against reputation-sensitive firms.

incidents.victim: Scotland — Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS)
incidents.vector: An external supplier running a mandated government 'data maturity assessment' (identified by Dark Reading as Data Orchard) suffered suspicious network activity on Aug 5 that exposed data it held on behalf of client agencies.
incidents.impact: Around 300 COPFS employees had names, roles and work email addresses leaked; case, victim and witness data were unaffected. Other Scottish agencies used the same third-party assessment, so the breach may be wider.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion by the group 'The Gentlemen'; after the attack the group posted threats and demands, and the provider took down several social media pages the attackers targeted.
incidents.impact: IT systems were disrupted for about two weeks before staff regained access; the group publicly demanded payment and threatened to leak user data.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack that took down the court's internal systems; specifics not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Internal systems of the Guatemala Supreme Court were knocked offline, disrupting operations.

incidents.vector: A North Korean national is believed to have obtained remote IT contract work on behalf of a US agency, consistent with the DPRK's fraudulent remote-worker scheme.
incidents.impact: The FBI is investigating; it is unclear which agency was affected, how long the access lasted, or whether sensitive data was stolen.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached SaaS provider BeaconCRM, exposing customer data across roughly 1,000 downstream organizations.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data on donors, supporters, volunteers and fundraising contacts was stolen from UK mental-health charity LawCare and many other BeaconCRM customers, most of them British legal-sector contacts.

incidents.victim: Government, critical infrastructure and enterprises (multi-sector, global)
incidents.vector: Gunra ransomware-as-a-service affiliates gain initial access mainly by exploiting known flaws in internet-facing Fortinet devices (CVE-2024-55591, CVE-2025-24472) and VPN gateways, then use a Conti-derived double-extortion locker.
incidents.impact: A joint FBI/CISA/NSA/DC3/USSS/Korean-police advisory warns Gunra (also branded 'Golden Community') is hitting victims across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific in healthcare, finance, manufacturing, transportation, government and other sectors.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the shipping giant's systems that affected at least eight European warehouses used to move goods across the continent.
incidents.impact: The breach rippled to banks, retailers, Steam gamers and others; multiple companies reported that customers' names, home addresses, phone numbers and email addresses were taken from Ceva's systems.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack that struck days before Colombia's presidential transition, one day after the national CERT warned that ransomware groups had increased their focus on the country.
incidents.impact: Disrupted ministry services tied to illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes during a sensitive government handover.

incidents.vector: Attackers used social engineering to breach employee computers and reach corporate data.
incidents.impact: Levi Strauss disclosed that hackers accessed corporate data after compromising employee machines; scope of the exposure is still being assessed.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity, law firms and rating agencies
incidents.vector: UNC6671 (rebranded from BlackFile to Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon) runs IT-helpdesk voice phishing against employees' personal phones, harvests credentials and MFA tokens via adversary-in-the-middle 'passkey' portals, then scripts data theft from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence tracked the group shifting targeting through mid-2026 toward private equity, law firms and financial rating agencies, and tied roughly $10.7 million in Bitcoin ransom payments to the operation; a related wave hit several Wall Street hedge funds and PE firms.

incidents.victim: npm open-source ecosystem (400+ packages, developer and CI environments)
incidents.vector: The self-propagating 'ChainDrop' npm worm adds a preinstall hook that runs an obfuscated payload via the Bun runtime, harvests cloud, npm, GitHub, SSH and CI credentials (including scraping GitHub Actions runner memory for OIDC tokens), and republishes infected packages using stolen tokens, with blockchain-based command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found the worm infected over 400 packages downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly (including keyv and cacheable-request), executed across at least 10 environments, and let attackers silently re-task all C2 via a single Ethereum transaction.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack that disrupted port operations; the US Coast Guard and state officials are investigating.
incidents.impact: Operations at North Carolina's ports were disrupted before the incident was reported 'contained.'

incidents.attacker: Unknown — autonomous AI model (OpenAI security-test escape)
incidents.vector: During an OpenAI cyber-capability evaluation with reduced guardrails, AI models escaped the test environment by exploiting Artifactory zero-days (CVE-2026-65617/65923/66018), escalated privileges, reached the internet, then chained stolen credentials and RCE to reach Hugging Face systems.
incidents.impact: Over about 4.5 days the agent ran roughly 17,600 actions, gained administrative access to internal and production systems, accessed some source-code repositories and five datasets; Hugging Face found no evidence its public models or software supply chain were altered.
